36.0.0.en: 1 O Lord, God of all, have mercy upon us, and behold us, and shew us the light of thy mercies. 2 And cast thy fear upon all the nations that have not sought after thee, that they may know that there is no God but thee, and declare thy great things. 3 Lift up thine hand against the strange nations, and let them know thy might. 4 As thou wast sanctified in us before them, so be thou magnified among them before us. 5 And let them know thee, as we have known thee, that there is no God but thee, O Lord. 6 Renew the signs, and work wonders. 7 Glorify thy hand and thy right arm. 8 Raise up indignation, and pour out wrath. 9 Destroy the adversary, and smite in sunder the enemy. 10 Hasten the time, and remember the covenant, and let them declare thy wondrous works. 11 Let him that escapeth be devoured by the fire of wrath, and let them that oppress thy people find destruction. 12 Smite in sunder the heads of the rulers of the enemies, that say, "There is none other but we." 13 Gather all the tribes of Jacob, and take them for thine inheritance, as from the beginning. 14 O Lord, have mercy upon the people that is called by thy name, and upon Israel, whom thou hast made equal to thy firstborn. 15 Have compassion on the city of thy sanctuary, Jerusalem, the city of thy rest. 16 Fill Zion that it may proclaim thy sayings. Fill thy people with thy glory. 17 Give testimony to those that are thy creation from the beginning, and raise up the prophecies that are in thy name. 18 Give reward to them that wait for thee, and let thy prophets be found true. Hear, O Lord, the prayer of them that supplicate unto thee, 19 according to the blessing of Aaron over thy people; that all the inhabitants of the earth may know that thou art the Lord, the God of the ages.

36.0.1.en: This prayer expresses the feelings of the people who were under oppression, but it is certainly not taken from the public rite which the people practiced; rather it is a prayer coming from the heart of Ben Sirach in the name of the suffering people who await the Savior of the whole world. St. Augustine sees that verses 1-4 are a prayer offered on behalf of the nations that they may enjoy the fear of the Lord, and this was fulfilled by the coming of the incarnate Word of God.

36.0.2.en: Have mercy on us, O Lord God of all, and behold us, and put Your fear upon all the nations [1].

36.0.3.en: This prayer came as an expression of intense pain, before the rise of the Maccabean revolt in 164 BC and the purification of the temple. The psalmist says: "God shall bless us; and all the ends of the earth shall fear him" (Ps 76:7).

36.1.0.en: Lift up Your hand against the strange nations, and allow them to see Your power [2].

36.1.1.en: By the strange nations he means those that despised Israel, and certain rulers, especially Antiochus Epiphanes, allowed them to offer unclean animals on the altar.

36.2.0.en: As You were sanctified in us before them, so be magnified in them before us [3].

36.2.1.en: This happened in former ages, as in the days of Moses the prophet, and now let this power appear once again, so that no wicked nation covets them and they say that their God has forgotten them. It is said: "Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I am against thee, O Zidon; and I will be glorified in the midst of thee: and they shall know that I am the LORD, when I shall have executed judgments in her, and shall be sanctified in her" (Ezek 28:22). The purpose of disciplining the nations is not vengeance, but enlightenment to know the Lord. It is a petition for the salvation of the nations. Would that they knew the true way! Would that they abandoned their idols!

36.2.2.en: St. Augustine often gave us examples confirming that the Lord's Prayer given in the Holy Gospel is characterized by comprehensiveness, for all the prayers found in the Old Testament have their counterparts in the Lord's Prayer, among them what is found in this chapter (36:4, 16).

36.2.3.en: v For example, he who says: "May You be sanctified in all men, as You are sanctified in us" (cf. Sir 36:16), what does he say but "Hallowed be thy name"?

36.2.4.en: And also he who says: "O God of hosts, turn us again, and cause thy face to shine; and we shall be saved" (Ps 80:3-4), what does he mean but: "Thy kingdom come."

36.2.5.en: And he who says: "Order my steps in thy word: and let not any iniquity have dominion over me" (Ps 119:133), what does he say but "Thy will be done, not my will"...

36.2.6.en: And he who says: "Let not the lust of gluttony nor fornication take hold of me" (cf. Sir 23:6), but "Bring us not into temptation"...

36.2.7.en: If you go through the words of the holy prayers, you will find nothing, in my way of thinking, that the Lord's Prayer does not include; therefore when we pray we are permitted to utter the same things but in different words, but it will not be permitted to say different things [1].

36.3.0.en: St. Augustine Let them know You as we know You, for there is no God but You, O Lord [4].

36.3.1.en: St. Augustine says: [This prophecy, in the mold of longing in the spirit of prayer, has been fulfilled in Christ Jesus, as we see[2].]

36.4.0.en: Renew Your signs, and work new wonders, and glorify Your hand and Your right arm [5].

36.4.1.en: By renewing the signs he means that the Lord should declare His wrath upon these nations, as He did of old to Pharaoh of Egypt, who humbled the people and refused to let them go out to the wilderness to offer sacrifice to the Lord (Ex 3:19-20).

36.5.0.en: Raise up Your wrath, and pour out Your indignation, and drive away the adversary, and destroy the enemy [6].

36.5.1.en: When we hear of the wrath and indignation of God it befits us to realize that God, who is all love, does not bear a spirit of vengeance, but is angry at evil, and longs for the purification of the sinner and his sanctification. When He sent Jonah the prophet to declare His wrath upon Nineveh because of its evils, the king and the leaders and the people returned to God with repentance, and so became a wonderful model through the generations of God's purpose in rebuke and discipline, namely His love for sinners that they return to the source of their sanctification.

36.5.2.en: In every age there were men of God among the pagan nations, such as righteous Job, who was the object of God's honoring him.

36.5.3.en: v You find many passages in Holy Scripture in which God is likened to the attributes of man. So if you ever hear the words "the wrath of God and His fury," do not think that wrath and fury are emotions and attributes present in God, but it is a way by which God condescends and speaks in order to discipline His children and set them right.

36.5.4.en: For we also, when we wish to guide our children and correct their faults, appear before them in a frightening form and with a stern and firm face which does not correspond to our true feelings, but corresponds to the manner of discipline.

36.5.5.en: If we always showed on our faces the tolerance and leniency that exists in our souls and inner feelings toward our children, without changing the features of our faces according to the children's behavior, we would spoil them and drive them to the worse. In this way we speak of the wrath of God: when it is said that God is angry, what is meant by this wrath is your repentance and your reform, for God in truth does not become angry or furious, but it is you who will bear the effects of wrath and fury when you fall into the terrible, harsh torments because of your sins and evils, in the case of God's disciplining you by what we call the wrath of God![3]

36.6.0.en: Origen Hasten the time, and remember Your oath, and let the people declare Your mighty works [7].

36.6.1.en: The oath mentioned here refers to the covenant which the Lord established with our father Abraham (Gen 17:21). Since the men of God in the Old Testament were awaiting the coming of the Messiah the Savior, who would fulfill the covenants established between God and men of faith, Ben Sirach asked that the time be hastened so that God might fulfill His promises, and God declare His mighty works through the Cross. At the same time Ben Sirach's prayer came expressing the bitterness of his soul at what the people of God were suffering at that time, while he enjoyed hope for the salvation of the nations from the corruption that had befallen them because of their unbelief.

36.7.0.en: Let him that escapeth be devoured by Your fiery wrath, and let him who harms Your people meet destruction [8].

36.7.1.en: If Ben Sirach asks for the swift coming of recompense upon the rulers who resisted the Lord and His people and who defiled the temple of the Lord, then by the spirit of prophecy he asks for the swift vengeance on the devil and his angels who oppose the kingdom of God in the hearts of mankind.

36.7.2.en: v We have fallen under the authority of our enemies, that is, "the king of this age" and his helpers of the powers of evil. For this reason our need became redemption by the One who buys us that we may return from the state of estrangement from Him. Our Savior gave His blood as a ransom for us... And since "the forgiveness of sins," which follows redemption, was impossible before man was set free, we must first be freed from the authority of him who took us captive and kept us under his control, and be freed beyond the reach of his hand, so that we may be able to obtain forgiveness of our sins and healing from the wounds of sin, so that we may accomplish works of piety and other virtues.

36.8.0.en: Origen Crush the heads of the leaders of the enemies, who say: "There is none other but we" [9].

36.8.1.en: Our life is a pleasant journey, even though it is full of trials and the resistance of the devil against us, but the Word of God became incarnate and dwelt among us and gave us by His Cross to crush the ancient serpent, the devil, according to His promise to Adam (Gen 3:15).

36.8.2.en: The psalmist stood amazed before the marvelous work of God, in the midst of the battle between God and the devil. He saw himself a sparrow with neither might nor power. He cannot escape from the snare of the fowlers, that is, the devil and his angels, but the Almighty helped him, and broke the snare for him and set him free. The psalmist sang, saying: "Our soul is escaped as a bird out of the snare of the fowlers: the snare is broken, and we are escaped. Our help is in the name of the LORD, who made heaven and earth" (Ps 124:7).

36.8.3.en: v What is the snare that was broken? The Apostle says: "(The Lord) shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly" (Rom 16:20), "that ye may recover yourselves out of the snare of the devil" (2 Tim 2:26). Behold, you see that Satan is the fowler, longing to catch our souls for destruction. Satan is the master of many snares and deceptions of every kind... When we are in the state of grace our souls are in safety. But as soon as we play with sin, our souls are troubled and become like a ship tossed by the waves [4].

36.9.0.en: St. Jerome Gather all the tribes of Jacob, and give them their inheritance as in the beginning [10].

36.9.1.en: Together with God's care for every individual personally, He seeks to gather the believers together from Adam to the end of the ages, to establish from them the Church, the queen and heavenly bride. The Apostle Paul says: "For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ" (2 Cor 11:2).

36.10.0.en: O Lord, have mercy on Your people who are called by Your name, and Israel whom You likened to Your firstborn son [11].

36.10.1.en: Although Cyrus the Persian permitted the Jews to return, few of them returned, in three waves, to the Holy Land, and some remained in Babylon, and many went to the Fertile Crescent, and some to Egypt or Ethiopia. Many Jews settled outside the Holy Land, especially on the shores of the Mediterranean. This dispersion of the people changed many features of the Jewish religion.

36.10.2.en: v What is said about Israel? "He who sees God." How did they see God who walked among them in the flesh, and they counted Him a man and killed Him?...

36.10.3.en: "His name is great in Israel." Do you wish to be Israel? Note that man of whom the Lord said: "Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!" (Jn 1:47). If the Israelite indeed is one in whom is no guile, then he in whom there is guile or falsehood is not an Israelite in truth [5].

36.11.0.en: St. Augustine Have compassion on the city of Your sanctuary, Jerusalem, the city of Your rest [12].

36.11.1.en: The Jews considered Jerusalem an icon of heaven (Isa 54:10) and the temple the point of meeting of the people with God, and Jerusalem was the focus of the gaze of all the Jews, wherever they were scattered about the world, for it is the city of the great King, the city of peace, the city of Melchizedek (Gen 14:18), the city of David the great king, and in the days of David and Solomon became the religious and political capital. The beloved city of Jerusalem was exposed throughout the ages to demolition, burning and defilement.

36.11.2.en: It became a symbol of heaven: "Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out: and I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, which is new Jerusalem, which cometh down out of heaven from my God" (Rev 3:12). "And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband" (Rev 21:2).

36.11.3.en: v Honor the holy Church and love her and praise her, your mother the heavenly Jerusalem, the city of God. She is the one that in this faith which she receives bears fruit and spreads throughout all the world. She is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth (1 Tim 3:15), which in her dispensing of the Sacraments bears with the wicked who at some time are cut off and excluded [6].

36.12.0.en: St. Augustine Fill Zion with the celebration of Your divine virtue, and Your people with Your glory [13].

36.12.1.en: In the Old Testament God was preparing Zion that He might become incarnate of St. Mary and offer salvation to the world. Now the Lord cares for His Church, the Zion of the New Testament, as the people of God who share with Him in the divine nature. The psalmist says: "The LORD loveth the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob" (Ps 87:2).

36.12.2.en: v It seems to me that the gates of Zion are the virtues.

36.12.3.en: As vice and sin are the two gates of death, I think that the gates of Zion are the virtues [7].

36.12.4.en: v He does not mean the gates that we see today in dust and ashes, but he means the gates against which hell shall not prevail (Mt 16:18), through which enter the multitudes of those who believe in Christ [8].

36.13.0.en: St. Jerome Bear witness to what You created in the beginning, and show forth the prophecies that were spoken in Your name [14].

36.14.0.en: Reward those who wait for You, and let Your prophets be found trustworthy [15].

36.14.1.en: The men of God in the Old Testament were awaiting the fulfillment of the prophecies concerning salvation and the coming of the Lord Christ. "And I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come: and I will fill this house with glory, saith the LORD of hosts. The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the LORD of hosts. The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith the LORD of hosts: and in this place will I give peace, saith the LORD of hosts" (Hag 2:7-9). St. John Chrysostom sees that the prophet uttered this statement because many of the Jews found it hard to believe how the old temple would return once again with its gold and silver after it had become dust and ashes, as though the Lord were saying to them: [Why do you not believe, for the silver is Mine and the gold is Mine, I do not need to borrow from anyone to adorn My house?![9]]

36.15.0.en: Hear, O Lord, the prayer of those who supplicate You, according to the blessing of Aaron upon Your people [16].

36.15.1.en: Ben Sirach concludes the prayer by asking for the blessing which He promised His people by the mouth of Aaron (Num 6:22-27). The Lord made clear that the blessing that comes upon the people through the priests is God's own gift, offered by the Holy Trinity, and the priests are but a means; they ask God three times that the Holy Trinity bless the people. Thus he affirms that it is He who blesses, not the priests, however high their rank; He keeps and has mercy and it is He who grants peace.

36.16.0.en: And let all the inhabitants of the earth know that You are the Lord, the God of the ages [17].

36.16.1.en: With Ben Sirach's concern for the service of the ancient people and prayer on their behalf, he does not ignore the salvation of the nations which is realized by the coming of the Messiah the Savior. Here he asks on behalf of "all the inhabitants of the earth."

36.17.s.en: 2. The need for a spirit of discernment

36.17.0.en: 20 The belly receiveth all meats, yet is one meat better than another. 21 The palate discerneth the meats of venison, and an heart of understanding discerneth false speeches. 22 A froward heart causeth heaviness: but a man of much experience will requite him.

36.17.1.en: The spirit of discernment is like food that the wise man tastes, and so is pleased with its flavor [18]. It gives sweetness to a man in every circumstance he lives in; he feels as though the sweetness that touches his inner being is unique, he has never experienced sweetness like it.

36.17.2.en: The stomach receives all kinds of food, but some food is better than another [18].

36.17.3.en: It is difficult for a man to give a definition of sweetness. It touches his food and drink and words. Material food is taken by the stomach, and the palate distinguishes it with a kind of sweetness that differs from one food to another and from one person to another. This sweetness gives a man a kind of discernment between one food and another.

36.17.4.en: As the palate tastes the flavor of venison, so the understanding heart discerns false speeches [19].

36.17.5.en: A man's palate discerns foods, and his heart and ear discern the speech which he utters with his tongue, and as it is said: "The ear trieth words, as the mouth tasteth his meat" (Job 12:11).

36.17.6.en: The wise man has a heart that discerns good, fitting speech from bad, unfitting speech. Therefore it befits a man not to be hasty in answering or commenting on a matter before his mind and heart examine it.

36.17.7.en: v He is not speaking of the ear of the body (Job 12:11), but the ear of the spirit. With the bodily ears we hear the sounds of words, but with the inner ears we discern thought and words. Likewise "the palate (especially the taste) tastes food," meaning that it appreciates it with respect to its pleasure. So also the palate of the spirit discerns its benefit.

36.17.8.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem v "For the mind nous discerns words"... If God gives us the palate to discern the tasting of food, He also gives us the mind to take our decisions, and time allows us to seek understanding.

36.17.9.en: St. John Chrysostom v There is one judge who oversees the inside, that is, the power of discernment which belongs to the mind, but through fitting ways that keep the five senses distinct. God works wonders, so the eye cannot hear, nor the ear see, nor the mouth smell, nor the nose taste, nor the hands smell. While all these work through the powers of the one mind, yet no sense can practice other than what the Creator has appointed for it. And so through these outward bodily arrangements, He leaves it to us to gather them within in a spiritual way...

36.17.10.en: While there is one wisdom dwelling in one man less than in another... yet in itself it bears no differences among them, but by it we practice various different operations, so one receives the gift of wisdom, and another the gift of knowledge, and another tongues, and another the gift of healing...

36.17.11.en: The blessed Job condemns the inexperience of his friends, and the insolence of everyone who is puffed up, claiming that he has learned in wisdom. For knowing something about God is one thing, and tasting what you know with understanding is another.

36.17.13.en: The crooked heart causes grief, and the man of wide experience requites it [20].

36.17.14.en: "The wicked heart," that is, the impure, brings many troubles upon a man. It is characterized by narrowness, so it cannot bear a word of criticism, and does not rejoice in giving, while the pure heart is spacious, longs to love even those who trouble it, and serves everyone, and is pleased with giving, not taking, therefore it reaps countless blessings.

36.18.s.en: 3. The spirit of discernment and the choice of a wife

36.18.0.en: 23 A woman will receive any man whatever, yet is one daughter better than another. 24 The beauty of a woman cheereth the countenance, and surpasseth all the desires of man. 25 And if there be mercy and meekness in her tongue, her husband is not like the other sons of men. 26 He that getteth a wife beginneth a possession, she is to him the head of riches, and a help meet for him, and a pillar of rest. 27 Where no hedge is, the possession is spoiled; and where no woman is, the wanderer mourneth. 28 Who will trust a thief well girded, that wandereth from city to city? so is the man that hath no nest, and lodgeth wheresoever the night overtaketh him.

36.18.1.en: In ancient times a woman had no opportunity to choose a husband, and if she had, as happened with Rebecca the wife of Isaac (Gen 24:1-8), it is not comparable with a man's freedom to choose his wife. Usually the parents or those in their place chose the husband and the wife; though this does not mean the deprivation of the spouses of happiness. And the rate of divorce was not high as it is today.

36.18.2.en: As much as he warned the young men lest they choose a wicked wife, he blesses him who marries one whose tongue is gentle and who is characterized by meekness; her husband feels that he is not like the rest of men, because he lives as with an angel from heaven [23].

36.18.3.en: He speaks of the importance of the good wife in her husband's life, declaring that she plays a principal role in his life:

36.19.0.en: a. Richer than anyone who has wealth [24], for she is a precious treasure (Prov 31:10).

36.19.1.en: b. He does not feel isolation, for she is a helper to him [24].

36.19.2.en: c. He counts her as a pillar on which he leans while in safety [24].

36.20.0.en: d. She encircles him like a hedge around him, so her husband does not wander [25].

36.21.0.en: e. He feels a stability, especially when he returns in the evening to his house and feels her presence with him [26-27].

36.21.1.en: A woman receives any son[10], but there is a daughter[11] better than another [21].

36.21.2.en: The beautiful woman makes the man happy, and surpasses all that he desires [22].

36.21.3.en: Here he praises physical beauty, which without doubt deserves praise, like everything beautiful among men or among creatures, yet all God's creatures are beautiful, and beauty is a relative matter, as there is a difference between physical beauty and the beauty of the spirit.

36.21.4.en: And if there is gentleness and meekness in her tongue, her husband is not like other men [23].

36.21.5.en: We can touch Ben Sirach's view of woman through his speaking of the role of the virtuous woman in her husband's life.

36.21.6.en: The tongue of the wicked wife, as we saw before, utterly destroys the husband's life, while the tongue of the virtuous wife offers the husband gentleness and meekness, and even lifts him above all men, that is, transforms him into the likeness of an angel.

36.21.7.en: Ben Sirach did not say this about the good husband in the effect of his tongue upon his wife. We have not heard that the good man by his tongue transforms his wife into something higher than all men.

36.21.8.en: There are other qualities worthy of the woman to be adorned with: such as wisdom, chastity of tongue and bearing responsibilities, those qualities that make the husband a happy person who boasts of her among his friends, for physical beauty may turn to ugliness because of illness, while the good constant qualities remain, and death does not destroy them.

36.21.9.en: He who marries such a woman has acquired the best possession, a helper like himself, and a pillar to lean on [24].

36.21.10.en: Ben Sirach exalts the wife in a wonderful way. For although she is often physically weak in relation to the man, yet she is able to lift him above all men, and make him rich by being his precious treasure, and even give him strength, as he leans on her in his weakness as on a pillar!

36.21.11.en: Where there is no hedge, possessions are plundered, and where there is no wife, the man wanders mourning [25].

36.21.12.en: A good marriage protects both parties, the husband and the wife, from the snares of the devil. Ben Sirach sees that marriage to a wise woman is better than celibacy, for the wife becomes to her husband a support and helper to him (Gen 2:18). A good woman is a good portion, given to him that feareth the Lord, whether rich or poor, his heart is in gladness and his countenance always bright.

36.21.13.en: Marriage may help a man to commit to a social life and to preserve his time, his money and his reputation, and not to deviate into harmful paths. The good woman is to him like a hedge, a guard and an overseer; he finds one who cares about his affairs, and fears for him, and the warmth of a happy quiet home will be waiting for him. It is natural that he who has no wife and no children moves easily from place to place and from house to house. This may push him to deviate and to instability.

36.21.14.en: Who will trust the armed thief who wanders from city to city? [26].

36.22.0.en: Who will trust the man who has no shelter, and lodges wherever the evening overtakes him [27].

36.22.1.en: Many look to marriage as a safe shelter for the wife, but Ben Sirach sees that in the virtuous wife the husband dwells in a safe house, in which he sleeps and rests!

36.23.0.en: v Look upon all mankind, for You are the God of all!

36.23.1.en: You were sanctified in Your believing children, and through You they became saints!

36.23.2.en: May You be glorified by the return of all the nations to You!

36.23.3.en: In Your love You are angry at their evils, and in Your compassion You draw them to You.

36.23.4.en: Hasten Your coming, that we may meet all the pious believers, and rejoice in Your presence among the heavenly and the earthly.

36.23.5.en: v You have kindled our hearts with longing to enjoy the Jerusalem above, our mother.

36.23.6.en: We see You, and so we are truly counted the heavenly Israel.

36.23.7.en: The prophecies are fulfilled by Your coming on the clouds.

36.23.8.en: And we enjoy what eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither hath entered into the heart of man!

36.23.9.en: v Grant me the spirit of discernment in all my life.

36.23.10.en: May I know what is good and fitting for me as Your son, and reject what is bad and unfitting for me.

36.23.11.en: By the spirit of discernment my heart is enlarged with love for all the sons of men, loving giving more than taking, and listening more than speaking; I reject the wicked one, so grief cannot slip into my heart, nor does my soul suffer disturbance.

36.23.12.en: v My God, truly the good wife makes her husband happy; he sees her as his treasure, his support and his hedge, so he finds stability with her, and by Your Holy Spirit the two become one flesh.

36.23.13.en: Let wisdom be the bride who embraces me.

36.23.14.en: Let wisdom occupy my heart, and I shall be in a wedding that never ceases.

36.23.15.en: Neither the events of the world, nor illnesses, nor all the powers of darkness can spoil my peace.

36.23.16.en: I shall not move from city to city, for heaven is my dwelling.

36.23.17.en: And no thief shall assault my mind or my heart or my feelings, for Your divine Kingdom is established within me!
